shortcut_findings.heuristic: Read only the original or first instrument.
shortcut_findings.result: Fails in both: keeps Elin Voss and Milo Hart together, misses Nia Bell, and falsely retains one displaced designation. It does recover the two offices and Ada Wynn.

Fails in both. If latest means last in supplied order or latest operative instrument, n5q2 names Nia Bell but cannot independently identify her trust or prove authority, and omits the unchanged edges. If latest means latest document date, h7m4 contributes no graph edge.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Union the designations from both instruments.
shortcut_findings.result: Fails in both even after a correct trust join: it retains both historical selectable names alongside Nia Bell and Ada Wynn. The extra edge is Elin Voss in D0 and Milo Hart in D1.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Treat the variation as superseding the principal instrument or the entire beneficiary section.
shortcut_findings.result: Fails in both. Whole-instrument supersession drops both offices and both surviving original beneficiary edges; whole-beneficiary-section supersession also drops both surviving original beneficiary edges, even if the offices are retained. Clause 5 and the signed operative wording limit the change to one provision.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Always replace the first beneficiary provision and preserve the rest.
shortcut_findings.result: Incidental exact full-graph match in D0, assuming the other edges and trust join are recovered correctly. Fails in D1: it drops Elin Voss and wrongly retains Milo Hart. Always replacing the second gives the converse incidental match and failure. Neither fixed choice tracks the locator.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Guess the only named trust, join by the common officer or retention recipient, or treat the title as a trust name.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Read the exact locator and reference, validate the signed replacement under clause 5, and preserve other provisions.
shortcut_findings.result: Succeeds on the full graph in both. Reading the locator with the original clause table alone is enough to predict the contrast in this controlled pair, but not to establish the signatures, authority, effective date or attached proof.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Use IDs, titles, headings, order or administrative dates as answer labels.
shortcut_findings.result: Fails to distinguish conditions because that material is fixed. The principal heading legitimately identifies the trust for execution-based proof; titles and ordering can flag record roles, not the replacement target. Signature on 8 October, advice-file supply on 19 October and meeting or cut-off on 23 October are not the operative date of 12 October.

Those materials disclose the answer or the contrast; they are not evidence at the cut-off.

Do not mask PI-67Q4, the locator, original provision numbers, instrument heading, powers, operative designation, signature, capacity or dates. These are substantive evidence, not answer leakage.

The fate of any pre-12 October entitlement of Elin Voss in D0 or Milo Hart in D1 is unresolved, not contradicted by silence.

With no affirmative contrary proposition, these are unsupported rather than explicitly contradicted.
